A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same framework. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original mesh-parameterization experiments, quantitative comparisons in Tables 1–2, and ablations in Appendix A.3.

after.justification: v2 retains these experiments and adds original user-study, packing, partitioning, and training-time results.

M1.justification: Appendix A.3 adds evaluated pipeline variants using PartField partitioning and Maya, Blender, or Houdini packing in place of existing components. These are optional adaptations; the default ShDF/grid pipeline, neural architecture, and training losses remain unchanged.

E1.justification: v2 adds human perceptual evaluation with 115 participants, comprising 45 industry experts and 70 general participants. This introduces population-based assessment of semantic alignment and seam visibility beyond v1's mesh metrics and qualitative renderings.

E2.justification: PartField joins ShDF and SAMesh in the partitioning comparison, and a new packing comparison evaluates Maya, Blender, and Houdini (Tables 5–6). The existing headline UV-parameterization comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: The new user study specifies 11 comparisons per participant: five semantic and six visibility questions, with separate expert/general reporting. Appendix A.3 also introduces a controlled seven-chart cow packing comparison using texel density and UV-space utilization, plus total and per-iteration training-time measurements. These supplement the retained evaluation protocols.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands supplementary analysis through packing-efficiency comparisons, PartField partitioning ablations, and computational-cost analysis identifying seam extraction as the main visibility-training bottleneck. The original semantic/visibility-objective ablation is retained as Table 7; its expanded discussion does not represent new measurements.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty estimates. The added preference percentages and timing averages provide new descriptive results without introducing uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: The existing headline scores remain unchanged: v1 Tables 1–2 become v2 Tables 1 and 3. New results include expert preferences of 93.70% for visibility-aware and 80.22% for semantic-aware outputs, PartField conformality/equiareality of 0.8999/0.6921, packing-efficiency measurements, and training-time comparisons. These are additional results, not same-setting performance improvements over v1.

T1.justification: Around Eq. 7, v2 corrects the contradictory local AO convention and loss reasoning: zero denotes occlusion and one exposure, so high-AO seams increase the loss. This aligns the reasoning with the existing Eq. 4 definition. The equations and remaining mathematical development are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about unsupervised semantic-aware and visibility-aware UV parameterization. The added evaluations support these existing claims.

C2.justification: v2 expands v1's brief assurances of minor geometric degradation into explicit discussion of distortion-versus-perception tradeoffs, partitioning effects, and the greater equiareality loss of global visibility optimization. Appendix A.3 adds qualifications about segmentation-dependent outcomes and substantial training overhead, alongside proposed computational remedies.

D1.justification: v2 newly reports total and per-iteration training times, explicitly distinguishes per-mesh training from inference, and discloses sequential per-part execution and inspection of 3–5 neighbors during seam detection. Existing architecture specifications and the code-access statement remain unchanged; hardware and detailed training budgets remain unspecified.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to PartField and Houdini for the new comparisons. Section 3.2 also explicitly disclaims backbone novelty and locates the contribution in integrating semantic and visibility objectives, clarifying the attribution already present in v1.

P1.justification: v2 introduces qualitative/quantitative subsections within Section 4, expands seam-detection explanations and Appendix A.3 discussion, and removes the acknowledgments. These are localized structural and prose revisions; the overall organization and most foundational exposition remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds preference and training-time tables, a packing table and visualization, and a questionnaire figure. The partitioning figures expand to include PartField rows and revised captions. Most earlier figures are retained unchanged, including those relocated or renumbered.

improvement.justification: The user study supplies direct human evidence for perceptual benefits that v1 supported through proxy metrics and renderings. Correcting the AO contradiction and documenting distortion and training-cost tradeoffs also materially improve correctness and transparency. Missing uncertainty estimates and incomplete timing controls limit the new evidence, but the gains in validation and practical understanding are substantial.
